messages.text:
The first real mismatch is a classic Windows trap: Python was encoding Unicode tree characters through the console codepage and translating newlines to CRLF, while the reference emits UTF-8 with LF.

I’m switching all observable output to explicit UTF-8 bytes with `\n`.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess, pathlib
ref=pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip()
checks=[['probe_dir','--color','never','--icons','never'],['probe_dir','-l','--color','never','--icons','never'],['probe_dir','-T','-L','2','--color','never','--icons','never'],['probe_dir','-a','--color','never','--icons','never'],['probe_dir','-F','always','--color','never','--icons','never'],['probe_dir','-l','--sort','size','--color','never','--icons','never'],['probe_dir','-l','--sort','oldest','--color','never','--icons','never']]
for args in checks:
    r=subprocess.run([ref]+args,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    p=subprocess.run(['python','eza_py.py']+args,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    print(' '.join(args), r.returncode==p.returncode, r.stdout==p.stdout, r.stderr==p.stderr)
    if r.stdout"'!=p.stdout:
        print('"'REF',r.stdout[:200]); print('PY ',p.stdout[:200])
'@ | python -"
